name: Nevado Sajama ridge drill site
science_objective: Drill the ridge-top Nevado Sajama bedrock, about 10 m from the hollow drill site, and run DAN to estimate the ridge's hydrogen (and by extrapolation water) content.
why_it_matters: NASA's team requested one drill target in a hollow and one on an adjacent ridge, only about 2 m apart in elevation, to compare their mineralogy, volatiles and organic chemistry.
position_source: PDS PLACES localized_interp.csv v42.0, frame ROVER, sol 4711, site 120, drive 82 (planetocentric_latitude, longitude; last ROVER row (sol 4711) before the sol 4718 image; next row is sol 4741). The same row is in localized_pos.csv, so it is a localized solution, not an interpolated one. This is where the rover was, not the surveyed position of the feature itself. Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.
ez_theme: Ridge drill site: paired with hollow

evidence.text: Blog sols 4716-4722: drilling finished on sol 4718 at Nevado Sajama on the ridge; MAHLI saw fine veins in both targets; DAN gathered hydrogen (by extrapolation, water) data for the ridge.
Blog sols 4709-4715: the boxwork group requested one drill in a hollow and one on an adjacent ridge; there is a mere 2-meter elevation difference between hollow floor and ridge top.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).
